system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-02-17, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/bysbij4-fog-alert-uae-motorists-warned-low-visibility] ABU DHABI, February 17, 2026 (WAM) – The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather warning regarding potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility across several western regions of the UAE. According to the NCM statement released on Tuesday, visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times—starting from 21:30 tonight until 10:00 AM Wednesday, February 18. The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads. Drivers are advised to follow all traffic safety guidelines, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles, and strictly adhere to modified speed limits, particularly in areas experiencing thick fog.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): Neither the English nor the Arabic phone text contains a protective action. Only the hazard, area, time and source are given, so the first page that handset users see does not tell them what to do. Fix: Add a short protective action right after the hazard in both languages, within the first page: for example 'Avoid driving; if you must, slow down, keep distance and use low-beam lights' and its Arabic equivalent. Move or shorten the source and date details if they push the action off page 1. [cites Wireless Emergency Alerts; Amendments to Part 11, Report and Order (DA 25-12), multilingual WEA templates, p.21]

data.headline: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero in western regions, 21:30 Tue 17 Feb to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb
data.description: FOG WARNING: Drive with extreme caution. Slow down, keep a safe distance and obey modified speed limits. Visibility may drop to zero in western regions of the UAE from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. Source: NCM.
data.instruction: If you are driving, take extreme care: slow down, keep a safe distance from other vehicles and strictly follow modified speed limits, especially in thick fog. Follow all traffic safety guidelines.
left_out: Reviewer's example actions 'Avoid driving' and 'use low-beam lights' were not used because they are not in the verified NCM statement. The phone text uses only the NCM advice: extreme caution, safe distance and modified speed limits.
No Arabic phone text was produced because this draft is in English only. The Arabic version still needs the same fix, with the protective action placed first.
The issuer site (https://alerts.example.ae) was not added to the phone text. This keeps the protective action and timing on page 1.
data.note_for_reviewer: I moved the protective action to the start of the phone text as requested. I limited it to NCM's own advice rather than the reviewer's 'avoid driving / low-beam lights' wording, which is not in the verified source. Please confirm that the operator's 'Western region (demo zone)' matches NCM's 'several western regions', and check whether Severe/Likely is the right level for potential zero-visibility fog.
